entries.title: Stock Market
entries.excerpt: The stock market is a complex social-economic system where shares of publicly held companies are issued, bought, and sold. It reflects collective investor sentiment, corporate performance, and macroeconomic conditions, and serves as a key mechanism for capital allocation and wealth creation.

entries.title: Share (Company Share)
entries.excerpt: A unit of ownership in a company, representing a claim on part of its assets and earnings.

entries.title: Production Chain Firm Operating Model
entries.excerpt: The actual structure, processes, and strategies by which a particular firm participates in and operates within a production chain, encompassing its sourcing, production, distribution, and coordination activities.

entries.title: Samuel David Alexander
entries.excerpt: Samuel 'Sami' David Alexander (13 July 1862 – 8 March 1943) was a Croatian Jewish industrialist, doyen of Croatian industrialists, a philanthropist and a member of the Zagreb prominent Alexander family. He played a central role in the industrial development of Croatia during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, and his philanthropic work left a lasting impact on Zagreb's cultural and educational institutions.

entries.title: Zagreb Stock Exchange
entries.excerpt: The Zagreb Stock Exchange (ZSE) is the principal securities exchange in Croatia, operating an electronic trading platform for equities, bonds, and other financial instruments. It serves as the primary marketplace for capital formation and secondary trading in the Croatian economy.

entries.title: Commercial Bank
entries.excerpt: A commercial bank is a financial institution that accepts deposits, offers checking and savings accounts, and provides loans to individuals and businesses. It operates within a regulatory framework, creates money through lending, and facilitates payments and credit intermediation.

entries.title: Investment Bank
entries.excerpt: A financial institution that provides capital market services including underwriting, merger and acquisition (M&A) advisory, sales and trading, asset management, and research. Investment banks serve as intermediaries between issuers of securities and the investing public, and they facilitate corporate financing, restructuring, and risk management.

entries.title: Universal Bank
entries.excerpt: A financial institution that offers a comprehensive range of banking services, including retail, commercial, investment, and wealth management, operating as a key intermediary in the financial system.

entries.title: Andritz AG
entries.excerpt: Andritz AG is an international technology group headquartered in Graz, Austria, providing plants, equipment, and services for the hydropower, pulp and paper, metals, and separation industries. It is one of the world's leading suppliers of electromechanical equipment and services for hydropower plants and a prominent player in the global pulp and paper machinery market.

entries.title: Food Industry Market
entries.excerpt: The market for goods and services related to the food industry, encompassing agricultural, processing, distribution, and retail activities.

entries.title: Cow Meat Market
entries.excerpt: A market for cow meat (beef) where buyers and sellers exchange beef products.

entries.title: Market Research
entries.excerpt: Systematic process of gathering, recording, and analyzing data about customers, competitors, and market conditions to inform business decisions.

entries.title: North East of England Process Industry Cluster
entries.excerpt: The North East of England Process Industry Cluster (NEPIC) is a regional cluster organization supporting the process industries in the North East of England, including chemicals, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, and related sectors.

entries.title: lululemon athletica inc.
entries.excerpt: Lululemon Athletica Inc. (LULU) is a publicly traded Canadian-American multinational retailer of athletic apparel and accessories, best known for its yoga-inspired clothing.

entries.title: Market Interaction Model
entries.excerpt: A conceptual representation of the dynamic exchanges, transactions, and coordination mechanisms that occur among buyers, sellers, and intermediaries within a market.

entries.title: Real Estate Market
entries.excerpt: The real estate market is the social institution and arena in which rights to land, buildings, and attached improvements are exchanged, including residential, commercial, industrial, and agricultural properties. It encompasses transactions, pricing, financing, regulation, and the activities of buyers, sellers, investors, developers, and intermediaries.

entries.title: Chemical Industries Association (CIA)
entries.excerpt: The Chemical Industries Association (CIA) is the leading trade association for chemical and pharmaceutical businesses in the United Kingdom, representing the interests of the sector to government, regulators, and the public.

entries.title: Retail
entries.excerpt: The activity of selling goods or services directly to consumers in relatively small quantities for personal use, rather than for resale.

entries.title: Misogyny
entries.excerpt: Misogyny refers to the hatred, contempt, or prejudice against women or girls. It is a system of beliefs, attitudes, and practices that devalue, degrade, and subordinate women, often embedded in cultural norms and institutional structures.

entries.title: Malandria
entries.excerpt: Malandria is a geographical and sociopolitical region, functioning as a distinct territorial unit within the broader social landscape.

entries.title: Profit
entries.excerpt: Financial surplus of revenue over costs realized by an economic actor, typically a firm, from production and exchange. Acts as a primary incentive and measure of efficiency in market economies.

entries.title: Market Interaction
entries.excerpt: The act of exchanging goods, services, or information between buyers and sellers in a market setting.

entries.title: Ownership Structure
entries.excerpt: The pattern of distribution of ownership rights and control over an organization or asset among different stakeholders.

entries.title: Private Military Co.
entries.excerpt: A private military company (PMC) is a for-profit organization that provides specialized military, security, and armed force services, often to governments, international organizations, or private clients.

entries.title: Energy Industry
entries.excerpt: The energy industry encompasses the extraction, conversion, distribution, and consumption of energy resources. It is a foundational economic domain that enables virtually all other productive activities, transportation, and daily life.

entries.title: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT)
entries.excerpt: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) is a Chinese semiconductor company focused on the design, development, and manufacturing of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips. It is part of China's efforts to build a domestic memory supply chain and reduce dependence on foreign memory suppliers.

entries.title: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
entries.excerpt: State-owned research and technology company in Finland providing research and innovation services to industry and society.

entries.title: Family
entries.excerpt: A fundamental social unit consisting of individuals related by blood, marriage, or adoption, functioning as a primary group for socialization, emotional support, and economic cooperation.

entries.title: Centro Brasileiro de Relações Internacionais
entries.excerpt: The Brazilian Center for International Relations (CEBRI) is an independent think tank dedicated to the analysis and debate of international affairs, focusing on Brazil's foreign policy, global governance, and regional integration.

entries.title: Gold Market
entries.excerpt: A market where gold is traded, including spot, futures, options, and exchange-traded products. Gold markets exist globally, with major hubs in London, New York, Shanghai, and Dubai, facilitating price discovery, hedging, and investment for central banks, financial institutions, miners, and individual investors.

entries.title: Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT)
entries.excerpt: A real estate investment trust (REIT) is a company that owns, operates, or finances income-producing real estate, allowing investors to pool capital for real estate investments.

entries.title: World Bank
entries.excerpt: International financial institution that provides loans and grants to governments of low- and middle-income countries for capital projects aimed at economic development and poverty reduction.

entries.title: Product Development Center
entries.excerpt: Organization whose mandate is product development: carrying a product from concept to validated, deliverable offer through product realization and technical method development.

Argentina
entries.excerpt: A federal presidential republic and the second-largest country in South America. Defined by its immigrant heritage, complex federal structure, and oscillation between developmentalist and neoliberal economic models.

entries.title: Australia
entries.excerpt: Australia is a federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy and the only country that is also a continent. A resource-exporting powerhouse deeply tied to Indo-Pacific demand, it combines mining and agriculture with advanced services, education exports and a large pension-capital pool. Six states and two territories share power under a stable federal system.

entries.title: Brazil
entries.excerpt: Brazil is a federal presidential republic in South America and the largest country in both area and population in the region. It possesses a diversified economy spanning agriculture, mining, manufacturing, and services, and plays a central geopolitical and ecological role due to the Amazon rainforest and its membership in major multilateral groupings.

entries.title: Canada
entries.excerpt: Canada is a federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy and the world's second-largest country by area. A Commonwealth realm with English-French bilingualism, it combines vast natural-resource endowments with an advanced services economy deeply integrated with the United States. Key sectors include energy, mining, forestry, banking and technology, under a decentralized federal system.

entries.title: China
entries.excerpt: China is Party-State polity in East Asia and the world's most populous major state. Governed by a single-party system under the Chinese Communist Party, it has transformed over the past four decades from a largely agrarian economy into a global industrial and technological power. China plays a central role in global manufacturing, trade, infrastructure development, and emerging technologies.

entries.title: Denmark
entries.excerpt: Denmark is a parliamentary constitutional monarchy in Northern Europe and a pioneer of wind energy. Its Nordic welfare model pairs flexible labor markets with broad social protection, while the economy specializes in pharmaceuticals, shipping, food and design. An EU member outside the eurozone, it anchors the Realm community with Greenland and the Faroe Islands.

entries.title: Dominican Republic
entries.excerpt: The Dominican Republic is a sovereign presidential republic on the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean, sharing its territory with Haiti. Historically shaped by sugarcane, mining, and tourism, it has evolved into a dynamic economy with strong remittance inflows, diversified services and industrial sectors, and growing investments in renewable energy and infrastructure.

entries.title: England
entries.excerpt: England is a constituent country of the United Kingdom located in Western Europe. It was the core territorial and institutional base of the early modern English state and later the British Empire. England played a central role in the Industrial Revolution, the development of parliamentary governance, common law traditions, and the formation of modern financial and industrial capitalism.

entries.title: Finland
entries.excerpt: Finland is a unitary parliamentary republic in Northern Europe and a global reference for education. Independent since 1917, it transformed from forestry dependence into an ICT and engineering economy led by Nokia-era successors, while retaining strong welfare institutions. EU and eurozone membership, plus 2023 NATO accession, frame its open, innovation-driven economy.

entries.title: France
entries.excerpt: France is a unitary semi-presidential republic and the European Union's second-largest economy. Combining a strong central state with global cultural influence, it leads in aerospace, luxury goods, nuclear energy and agriculture. EU integration, high public investment and a large welfare state shape its coordinated market economy.

entries.title: Hong Kong
entries.excerpt: Hong Kong is a Special Administrative Region of the People’s Republic of China, located on the southern coast of China. It has a highly developed, service-oriented economy, historically rooted in trade, finance, and logistics. Hong Kong is a major global financial center and port, with strong legal and regulatory institutions inherited from its colonial history under the United Kingdom. In recent years, there has been a push to develop technology and innovation sectors alongside traditional …

entries.title: India
entries.excerpt: India is a sovereign federal parliamentary republic in South Asia and the world’s most populous country. It combines a long civilizational history with modern constitutional governance established in 1950. India has a structurally diversified economy spanning agriculture, manufacturing, and a globally competitive services and technology sector, and plays an increasingly central role in Indo-Pacific geopolitics and multilateral institutions.

entries.title: Indonesia
entries.excerpt: Indonesia is a sovereign archipelagic republic in Southeast Asia composed of more than 17,000 islands. It is the world’s largest Muslim-majority country and one of the most populous nations globally. Indonesia has a diversified economy based on natural resources, manufacturing, and services, and plays a central geopolitical role within ASEAN and the broader Indo-Pacific region.

entries.title: Ireland
entries.excerpt: Ireland is a sovereign parliamentary republic in Western Europe occupying most of the island of Ireland. Since the late 20th century, it has transformed into a high-income, small open economy characterized by strong foreign direct investment inflows, a competitive corporate tax regime, and specialization in pharmaceuticals, information technology, and financial services within the European Union framework.

entries.title: Israel
entries.excerpt: Israel is a unitary parliamentary republic in the Middle East known for its technology and defense sectors. Founded in 1948, it built a startup-nation economy on R&D intensity, venture capital and military-civilian technology transfer, alongside strengths in water, agriculture and diamonds. Regional conflict and disputed borders remain central to its political economy.

entries.title: Italy
entries.excerpt: Italy is a unitary parliamentary republic and a founding member of the European Communities. Its economy pairs northern industrial districts — machinery, automotive, fashion — with a vast cultural-heritage tourism sector and persistent southern structural challenges. A G7 economy in the eurozone, it balances manufacturing excellence with high public debt and demographic aging.

entries.title: Japan
entries.excerpt: Japan is a parliamentary constitutional monarchy and one of the world's largest economies. Postwar industrial policy produced global leaders in automotive, electronics and robotics, organized around keiretsu networks and coordinated business-government councils. It now navigates rapid demographic aging, high public debt and energy import dependence while leading in automation and materials science.

entries.title: Malaysia
entries.excerpt: Malaysia is a federal constitutional monarchy in Southeast Asia composed of Peninsular Malaysia and East Malaysian states on the island of Borneo. Since independence, it has transitioned from a commodity-based economy to an export-oriented manufacturing and services hub, with strong specialization in electronics, palm oil, and petroleum, supported by industrial policy and integration into regional and global value chains.

entries.title: Mexico
entries.excerpt: Mexico is a federal presidential republic and Latin America's second-largest economy. Deeply integrated with the United States through USMCA supply chains, it is a manufacturing hub for automotive, electronics and aerospace alongside oil, mining and massive remittance inflows. Thirty-one states plus Mexico City share power in a democratic federal system consolidated since 2000.

entries.title: Netherlands
entries.excerpt: The Netherlands is a constitutional monarchy in Western Europe known for its advanced, trade-oriented economy and long-standing maritime and commercial tradition. Historically central to early modern global trade and finance, it remains a major logistics and distribution hub within Europe, with strong sectors in agriculture, chemicals, high-tech manufacturing, and financial services.

entries.title: New Zealand
entries.excerpt: New Zealand is a sovereign island nation in Oceania composed primarily of the North and South Islands. It operates as a parliamentary democracy and constitutional monarchy. Historically shaped by Māori settlement and later British colonization, New Zealand developed a high-income, export-oriented economy centered on agriculture, agri-technology, tourism, and services, with strong institutional quality and regulatory transparency.

entries.title: Ottoman Empire
entries.excerpt: The Ottoman Empire (1299–1922) was a transcontinental Islamic empire centered on Anatolia, the Balkans and the Middle East, ruled by a sultan-caliph from Constantinople. At its early modern peak it commanded major Eurasian trade routes and a tributary provincial order. Military defeat, nationalist secessions and World War I reduced it to Anatolia, ending with the Turkish Republic's proclamation in 1923. Figures below are a c.1914 snapshot.

entries.title: Portugal
entries.excerpt: Portugal is a unitary semi-presidential republic on the Iberian Peninsula's Atlantic edge and one of Europe's oldest nation-states. Pioneer of the Age of Discovery with a deep seafaring and mercantile tradition, it moved from dictatorship to democracy with the 1974 Carnation Revolution and joined the European Communities in 1986. Its open economy leans on services, tourism, cork, wine and olive oil, with fast-growing technology and renewable-energy sectors.

entries.title: Scotland
entries.excerpt: Scotland is a devolved nation within the United Kingdom with its own parliament, legal system and distinct cultural identity. Center of the Enlightenment and nineteenth-century heavy industry, it now blends North Sea energy, whisky and food exports, financial services in Edinburgh, and growing renewables. Devolution since 1999 gives Holyrood powers over health, education and justice.

entries.title: Singapore
entries.excerpt: Singapore is a sovereign city-state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula and one of the world's leading trade and financial hubs. Independent since 1965 after separation from Malaysia, it built prosperity on its strategic strait-side port, rule of law, and openness to capital and talent. Its advanced economy centers on shipping and logistics, financial services, electronics and petrochemicals, with a state-guided development model.

entries.title: South Korea
entries.excerpt: South Korea is a sovereign presidential republic in East Asia located on the southern portion of the Korean Peninsula. Following the Korean War, it transitioned from a low-income agrarian economy to a high-income, export-oriented industrial and technological power. Its development model combined state-led industrial policy, chaebol-centered conglomerate growth, human capital accumulation, and deep integration into global value chains.

entries.title: Spain
entries.excerpt: Spain is a parliamentary constitutional monarchy in Southern Europe and one of the eurozone's largest economies. Restored to democracy after Franco's death in 1975 and an EU member since 1986, it is organized as a highly decentralized state of autonomous communities. Tourism, automotive manufacturing, banking and renewable energy anchor an open, services-led economy.

entries.title: Sweden
entries.excerpt: Sweden is a constitutional monarchy in Northern Europe characterized by a high-income, export-oriented economy and a comprehensive welfare state. Historically transitioning from agrarian society to industrial power in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, Sweden developed globally competitive firms in engineering, automotive, telecommunications, and life sciences, supported by strong institutions, human capital formation, and social partnership models.

entries.title: Switzerland
entries.excerpt: Switzerland is a neutral federal republic renowned for direct democracy, banking and precision industries. Its consensus-driven cantonal federalism underpins political stability and openness, hosting global finance, pharmaceuticals, watchmaking and commodity trading. Outside the EU but deeply integrated via bilateral accords, it runs persistent surpluses on high-value services and manufacturing.

entries.title: Thailand
entries.excerpt: Thailand is a constitutional monarchy in Southeast Asia with a diversified, export-oriented economy. Historically the Kingdom of Siam, it avoided formal colonization and underwent gradual modernization in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Since the late 20th century, Thailand has developed strong manufacturing sectors—particularly automotive and electronics—alongside tourism and agro-industrial exports, integrated into regional and global value chains.

entries.title: United Arab Emirates
entries.excerpt: The United Arab Emirates is a federal monarchy of seven emirates on the Arabian Gulf's southern shore. Since federation in 1971, oil wealth has funded diversification into finance, aviation, logistics and tourism, with Dubai and Abu Dhabi as global hubs. Its open, expatriate-majority economy pairs sovereign-wealth investment with ambitious technology and energy-transition bets.

entries.title: United States
entries.excerpt: The United States is a federal presidential republic and the world's largest economy, spanning North America from the Atlantic to the Pacific. Founded on constitutional federalism with separation of powers, it became the center of twentieth-century industrial, financial and technological power. Its economy leads in technology, capital markets, higher education and defense industries, with the dollar as the global reserve currency.

entries.title: Uruguay
entries.excerpt: Uruguay is a sovereign presidential republic in South America located between Brazil and Argentina along the Atlantic coast. Historically shaped by livestock-based exports and early welfare-state development, it has evolved into a relatively stable democracy with strong institutions, diversified agricultural exports, growing services sectors, and a high share of renewable energy generation in its electricity matrix.

entries.title: Vietnam
entries.excerpt: Vietnam is a One-Party State polity located in Southeast Asia, bordered by China, Laos, and Cambodia, with an extensive coastline along the South China Sea. It operates under a one-party system led by the Communist Party of Vietnam. Historically shaped by Chinese rule, French colonization, and the Vietnam War, the country has transitioned into a rapidly growing emerging economy with key sectors including agriculture, manufacturing, electronics, and services. Institutional development and …

entries.title: Serbia
entries.excerpt: Serbia is a parliamentary republic in Southeastern Europe, successor of the Yugoslav federation, with Belgrade at the confluence of the Danube and Sava. It is an upper-middle-income economy reorienting from state industry toward automotive components, food processing, and ICT services, carried by a deep engineering tradition: the Mihajlo Pupin Institute's automation and computing lineage, the VINCA nuclear institute, and a university system anchored by the University of Belgrade. EU candidacy …

entries.title: Poland
entries.excerpt: Poland is a parliamentary republic in Central Europe and the largest economy in the Visegrad Group, known for one of the fastest sustained growth records in the European Union. Its post-1989 transition from a centrally planned to a market economy produced a diversified industrial base in automotive, machinery, chemicals and food processing, deep integration into European and German-led value chains, and a growing business-services sector.

entries.title: Soviet Union
entries.excerpt: The Soviet Union (USSR, 1922–1991) was a federal Marxist–Leninist one-party socialist state spanning Eurasia, built on a command economy and ruled by the Communist Party from Moscow until its dissolution into fifteen sovereign republics.

entries.title: Reality
entries.excerpt: The ontological substrate comprising physical, chemical, biological, informational, and social structures that constrain and respond to technical intervention.

entries.title: Action Interface & Actuation
entries.excerpt: The motoric and encoding boundary through which an agent imparts energy, information, or structure onto reality.

entries.title: Concrete Technical Artifact
entries.excerpt: A specific, fully-specified object, system, or code module that has been produced or operated; the primary carrier of technical effect.

entries.title: Technical Blueprint
entries.excerpt: Generative description that prescribes how to create, assemble, or configure an artifact.

entries.title: Technical Agent

entries.title: Technical Process

entries.title: Technical Standard

entries.title: Technical Constraint

entries.title: Technical Infrastructure

entries.title: Technical Feedback
entries.excerpt: Signal that indicates real-world effect of a technical act, enabling adjustment and error correction.

entries.title: Technical Act
entries.excerpt: Primitive, non-decomposable operation that a technical agent performs on reality or an artifact.

entries.title: Technical Principle
entries.excerpt: Foundational design law, operating axiom, or reliability rule governing technical interventions.

entries.title: Technical Strategy
entries.excerpt: Context-sensitive, resource-aware regime of planning and decision-making organizing technical work.

entries.title: Technical Framework
entries.excerpt: Overarching problem-structuring and solution-generation logic within which technical agents interpret requirements and synthesize artifacts.

entries.title: Technical Operator
entries.excerpt: Formal, procedural, or physical mechanism used to transform, assemble, verify, or maintain technical artifacts.

entries.title: Production Technical Object
entries.excerpt: Final deployable artifact that fulfills ultimate technical purpose in its operational environment.

entries.title: Constitutive Technical Object
entries.excerpt: Intermediate artifact, component, or sub-assembly serving as building block within a larger production object.

entries.title: Technique
entries.excerpt: Generalized, culturally transmitted body of knowledge regarding how to achieve a specific type of technical effect.

entries.title: Operative Technique
entries.excerpt: Context-specific, situated application of a generalized technique by a technical agent.

entries.title: Constitutive Technique
entries.excerpt: Specialized methods dedicated to creation, testing, and integration of constitutive technical objects.

entries.title: Technical Purpose
entries.excerpt: Teleological orientation of an artifact or process; the intended ultimate impact on reality, human experience, or a broader system.

entries.title: Technical Architecture
entries.excerpt: Fundamental structural organization of a system, embodied in its components, their relationships, and design principles.

entries.title: Technical Specification
entries.excerpt: Precise, quantitative statement of technical requirements, performance parameters, and interface conditions.

entries.title: Technical Evolution
entries.excerpt: Cumulative historical trajectory of change in technical artifacts, processes, or knowledge over time.

entries.title: Technical Labor
entries.excerpt: Purposive expenditure of human cognitive and physical effort applied to technical processes.

entries.title: Technical Institution
entries.excerpt: Formalized, durable social structures that organize, govern, incentivize, and sustain technical practice.

entries.title: Technical Research
entries.excerpt: Systematic investigation aimed at discovering new technical principles, materials, processes, or capabilities.

entries.title: Technical Competence
entries.excerpt: Embodied, acquired capacity of a technical agent to reliably execute technical processes and operative techniques.

entries.title: Technical Failure
entries.excerpt: State or event wherein an artifact or process deviates from its technical specification or required function.

entries.title: Technical Requirement
entries.excerpt: Formalized desired state, need, or performance objective that initiates technical practice.

entries.title: Verification
entries.excerpt: Systematic process to evaluate whether an artifact fulfills its technical specification or blueprint.

entries.title: Maintenance

entries.title: Security

entries.title: Resource

entries.title: Technical Obsolescence

entries.title: Relational Database Management System (RDBMS)
entries.excerpt: A specialized class of data systems that provides structured, persistent, and transactional storage with a formal data model (e.g., relational, document, graph). Database systems expose query languages, indexing mechanisms, concurrency control, and recovery protocols to ensure reliable access and manipulation of data by multiple agents.

entries.title: Technical Problem
entries.excerpt: A structured discrepancy between a current or projected state of Reality and a desired Technical Function, Specification, or Purpose. It defines the precise boundary of necessary intervention—arising from an unmet Technical Requirement, a Technical Failure, or the friction of Technical Constraints—and serves as the primary catalyst that compels a Technical Agent to initiate a Technical Process.

entries.title: 1112 — Vegetable and Melon Farming
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) growing vegetable and/or melon crops; (2) producing vegetable and/or melon seeds; and (3) growing vegetable and/or melon bedding plants. Climate and cultural practices limit producing areas but often permit the growing of a combination of crops in a year.

entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in the commercial catching or taking of finfish (e.g., bluefish, salmon, trout, tuna) from their natural habitat.

entries.title: 114112 — Shellfish Fishing
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in the commercial catching or taking of shellfish (e.g., clams, crabs, lobsters, mussels, oysters, sea urchins, shrimp) from their natural habitat.

entries.title: 114119 — Other Marine Fishing
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in the commercial catching or taking of marine animals (except finfish and shellfish).

entries.title: 11421 — Hunting and Trapping

entries.title: 114210 — Hunting and Trapping
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) commercial hunting and trapping; (2) operating commercial game preserves, such as game retreats; and (3) operating hunting preserves.

entries.title: 115 — Support Activities for Agriculture and Forestry
entries.excerpt: Industries in the Support Activities for Agriculture and Forestry subsector provide support services that are an essential part of agricultural and forestry production. These support activities may be performed by the agriculture or forestry producing establishment or conducted independently as an alternative source of inputs required for the production process for a given crop, animal, or forestry industry. Establishments that primarily perform these activities independent of the agriculture …

entries.title: 1151 — Support Activities for Crop Production
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing support activities for growing crops.

entries.title: 11511 — Support Activities for Crop Production
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing support activities for growing crops.

entries.title: 115111 — Cotton Ginning
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in ginning cotton.

Bracing of orchard trees and vines
Chemical treatment of soil for crops

entries.title: 115113 — Crop Harvesting, Primarily by Machine
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in mechanical harvesting, picking, and combining of crops, and related activities. The machinery used is provided by the servicing establishment.

entries.title: 115114 — Postharvest Crop Activities (except Cotton Ginning)
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in performing services on crops, subsequent to their harvest, with the intent of preparing them for market or further processing. These establishments provide postharvest activities, such as crop cleaning, sun drying, shelling, fumigating, curing, sorting, grading, packing, and cooling.

entries.title: 115115 — Farm Labor Contractors and Crew Leaders
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in supplying labor for agricultural production or harvesting.

entries.title: 115116 — Farm Management Services
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing farm management services on a contract or fee basis usually to citrus groves, orchards, or vineyards. These establishments always provide management and may arrange or contract for the partial or the complete operations of the farm establishment(s) they manage. Operational activities may include cultivating, harvesting, and/or other specialized agricultural support activities.

entries.title: 1152 — Support Activities for Animal Production
entries.excerpt: See industry description for 115210.

entries.title: 11521 — Support Activities for Animal Production

entries.title: 115210 — Support Activities for Animal Production
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in performing support activities related to raising livestock (e.g., cattle, goats, hogs, horses, poultry, sheep). These establishments may perform one or more of the following: (1) breeding services for animals, including companion animals (e.g., cats, dogs, pet birds); (2) pedigree record services; (3) boarding horses; (4) dairy herd improvement activities; (5) livestock spraying; and (6) sheep dipping and shearing.

entries.title: 115310 — Support Activities for Forestry
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in performing particular support activities related to timber production, wood technology, forestry economics and marketing, and forest protection. These establishments may provide support activities for forestry, such as estimating timber, forest firefighting, forest pest control, treating burned forests from the air for reforestation or on an emergency basis, and consulting on wood attributes and reforestation.

entries.title: 21 — Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
entries.excerpt: The Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction sector comprises establishments that extract naturally occurring mineral solids, such as coal and ores; liquid minerals, such as crude petroleum; and gases, such as natural gas. The term "mining" is used in the broad sense to include quarrying, well operations, beneficiating (e.g., crushing, screening, washing, and flotation), and other preparation customarily performed at the mine site, or as a part of mining activity. The Mining, Quarrying, …

entries.title: 211 — Oil and Gas Extraction
entries.excerpt: Industries in the Oil and Gas Extraction subsector operate and/or develop oil and gas field properties. Operation and development activities include exploration for crude petroleum and natural gas; drilling, completing, and equipping wells; operating separators, emulsion breakers, desilting equipment, and field gathering lines for crude petroleum and natural gas; and all other activities in the preparation of oil and gas up to the point of shipment from the producing property. This subsector …

entries.title: 2111 — Oil and Gas Extraction
entries.excerpt: Oil and Gas Extraction includes Crude Petroleum Extraction, and Natural Gas Extraction.

entries.title: 21112 — Crude Petroleum Extraction
entries.excerpt: See industry description for 211120.

entries.title: 211120 — Crude Petroleum Extraction
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) the exploration, development, and/or the production of petroleum from wells in which the hydrocarbons will initially flow or can be produced using normal or enhanced drilling and extraction techniques or (2) the production of crude petroleum from surface shales or tar sands or from reservoirs in which the hydrocarbons are semisolids. Establishments in this industry operate oil wells on their own account or for others on a contract …

entries.title: 21113 — Natural Gas Extraction
entries.excerpt: See industry description for 211130.

entries.title: 211130 — Natural Gas Extraction
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) the exploration, development, and/or the production of natural gas from wells in which the hydrocarbons will initially flow or can be produced using normal or enhanced drilling and extraction techniques or (2) the recovery of liquid hydrocarbons from oil and gas field gases. Establishments primarily engaged in sulfur recovery from natural gas are included in this industry.

entries.title: 212 — Mining (except Oil and Gas)
entries.excerpt: Industries in the Mining (except Oil and Gas) subsector primarily engage in mining, mine site development, and beneficiating (i.e., preparing) metallic minerals and nonmetallic minerals, including coal. The term "mining" is used in the broad sense to include ore extraction, quarrying, and beneficiating (e.g., crushing, screening, washing, sizing, concentrating, and flotation), customarily done at the mine site. Beneficiation is the process whereby the extracted material is reduced to particles …

entries.title: 2121 — Coal Mining
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) mining bituminous coal, anthracite coal, and lignite by underground mining, auger mining, strip mining, culm bank mining, and other surface mining; (2) developing coal mine sites; and (3) beneficiating (i.e., preparing) coal (e.g., cleaning, washing, screening, and sizing).

entries.title: 21211 — Coal Mining
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) mining bituminous coal, anthracite coal, and lignite by underground mining, auger mining, strip mining, culm bank mining, and other surface mining; (2) developing coal mine sites; and (3) beneficiating (i.e., preparing) coal (e.g., cleaning, washing, screening, and sizing).

tags: Bituminous coal or anthracite underground mine site development for own account

Coal, bituminous or anthracite, underground mining

entries.title: 2122 — Metal Ore Mining
entries.excerpt: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in developing mine sites or mining metallic minerals, and establishments primarily engaged in ore dressing and beneficiating (i.e., preparing) operations, such as crushing, grinding, washing, drying, sintering, concentrating, calcining, and leaching. Beneficiating may be performed at mills operated in conjunction with the mines served or at mills, such as custom mills, operated separately.

entries.title: 21221 — Iron Ore Mining
entries.excerpt: See industry description for 212210.

entries.title: 212210 — Iron Ore Mining
tags: Iron ore (e.g., hematite, magnetite, siderite, taconite) mining and/or beneficiating
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) developing mine sites, mining, and/or beneficiating (i.e., preparing) iron ores and manganiferous ores valued chiefly for their iron content and/or (2) producing sinter iron ore (except iron ore produced in iron and steel mills) and other iron ore agglomerates.

entries.title: 21222 — Gold Ore and Silver Ore Mining
entries.excerpt: See industry description for 212220.

Bullion, silver, produced at the mine
Gold ore mine site development for own account

Establishments primarily engaged in the transformation of the gold and silver into bullion or dore bar in combination with mining activities are included in this industry.

entries.title: 21223 — Copper, Nickel, Lead, and Zinc Mining
entries.excerpt: See industry description for 212230.

entries.title: 212230 — Copper, Nickel, Lead, and Zinc Mining
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in developing the mine site, mining, and/or beneficiating (i.e., preparing) ores valued chiefly for their copper, nickel, lead, or zinc content. Beneficiating includes the transformation of ores into concentrates. Establishments primarily engaged in recovering copper concentrates by the precipitation, leaching, or electrowinning of copper ore are included in this industry.

entries.title: 21229 — Other Metal Ore Mining
entries.excerpt: See industry description for 212290.

entries.title: 212290 — Other Metal Ore Mining
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in developing the mine site, mining, and/or beneficiating (i.e., preparing) metal ores (except iron and manganiferous ores valued for their iron content, gold ore, silver ore, copper, nickel, lead, and zinc ore).

entries.title: 2123 — Nonmetallic Mineral Mining and Quarrying
entries.excerpt: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in developing mine sites, or in mining or quarrying nonmetallic minerals (except fuels). Also included are certain well and brine operations, and preparation plants primarily engaged in beneficiating (e.g., crushing, grinding, washing, and concentrating) nonmetallic minerals. Beneficiation is the process whereby the extracted material is reduced to particles which can be separated into mineral and waste, the former suitable for …

entries.title: 21231 — Stone Mining and Quarrying
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises (1) establishments primarily engaged in developing the mine site, mining or quarrying dimension stone (i.e., rough blocks and/or slabs of stone), or mining and quarrying crushed and broken stone and/or (2) preparation plants primarily engaged in beneficiating stone (e.g., crushing, grinding, washing, screening, pulverizing, and sizing).

entries.title: 212311 — Dimension Stone Mining and Quarrying
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in developing the mine site and/or mining or quarrying dimension stone (i.e., rough blocks and/or slabs of stone).

entries.title: 212319 — Other Crushed and Broken Stone Mining and Quarrying

Boulder crushed and broken mining and/or beneficiating
Diabase crushed and broken stone mining and/or beneficiating

entries.title: 21232 — Sand, Gravel, Clay, and Ceramic and Refractory Minerals Mining and Quarrying
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises (1) establishments primarily engaged in developing the mine site and/or mining, quarrying, dredging for sand and gravel, or mining clay (e.g., china clay, paper clay and slip clay) or ceramic and refractory minerals and (2) preparation plants primarily engaged in beneficiating (e.g., washing, screening, and grinding) sand and gravel, clay, and ceramic and refractory minerals.

entries.title: 212321 — Construction Sand and Gravel Mining
tags: Construction sand and gravel beneficiating (e.g., grinding, screening, washing)

entries.title: 212322 — Industrial Sand Mining
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one or more of the following: (1) operating industrial grade sand pits; (2) dredging for industrial grade sand; and (3) washing, screening, or otherwise preparing industrial grade sand.

entries.title: 212323 — Kaolin, Clay, and Ceramic and Refractory Minerals Mining
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises (1) establishments primarily engaged in developing the mine site and/or mining clay (e.g., china clay, paper clay and slip clay) or ceramic and refractory minerals and (2) establishments primarily engaged in beneficiating (i.e., preparing) clay or ceramic and refractory minerals.

entries.title: 21239 — Other Nonmetallic Mineral Mining and Quarrying
entries.excerpt: See industry description for 212390.

entries.title: 213 — Support Activities for Mining

Establishments performing exploration for minerals, on a contract or fee basis, are included in this subsector. Exploration services include traditional …

entries.title: 2131 — Support Activities for Mining
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing support services, on a contract or fee basis (except geophysical surveying and mapping, mine site preparation, construction, and transportation activities), required for the mining and quarrying of minerals and for the extraction of oil and gas. Drilling, taking core samples, and making geological observations at prospective sites for minerals, on a contract or fee basis, are included in this industry.

entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing support services, on a contract or fee basis (except geophysical surveying and mapping, mine site preparation, construction, and transportation activities), required for the mining and quarrying of minerals and for the extraction of oil and gas. entries.title: 22 — Utilities
entries.excerpt: The Utilities sector comprises establishments engaged in the provision of the following utility services: electric power, natural gas, steam supply, water supply, and sewage treatment and disposal. Within this sector, the specific activities associated with the utility services provided vary by utility: electric power includes generation, transmission, and distribution; natural gas includes distribution; steam supply includes provision and/or distribution; water supply includes treatment and …

entries.title: 221 — Utilities
entries.excerpt: Industries in the Utilities subsector provide electric power, natural gas, steam supply, water supply, and sewage treatment and disposal through a permanent infrastructure of lines, mains, and pipes. Establishments are grouped together based on the utility service provided and the particular system or facilities required to perform the service.

entries.title: 2211 — Electric Power Generation, Transmission and Distribution
entries.excerpt: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in generating, transmitting, and/or distributing electric power. Establishments in this industry group may perform one or more of the following activities: (1) operate generation facilities that produce electric energy; (2) operate transmission systems that convey the electricity from the generation facility to the distribution system; and (3) operate distribution systems that convey electric power received from the generation …

entries.title: 22111 — Electric Power Generation
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating electric power generation facilities. These facilities convert other forms of energy, such as water power (i.e., hydroelectric), fossil fuels, nuclear power, and solar power, into electrical energy. The establishments in this industry produce electric energy and provide electricity to transmission systems or to electric power distribution systems.

entries.title: 221111 — Hydroelectric Power Generation
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating hydroelectric power generation facilities. These facilities use water power to drive a turbine and produce electric energy. The electric energy produced in these establishments is provided to electric power transmission systems or to electric power distribution systems.

entries.title: 221112 — Fossil Fuel Electric Power Generation
tags: Electric power generation, fossil fuel (e.g., coal, oil, gas)
Power generation, fossil fuel (e.g., coal, gas, oil), electric
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating fossil fuel powered electric power generation facilities. These facilities use fossil fuels, such as coal, oil, or gas, in internal combustion or combustion turbine conventional steam process to produce electric energy. The electric energy produced in these establishments is provided to electric power transmission systems or to electric power distribution systems.

entries.title: 221113 — Nuclear Electric Power Generation
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating nuclear electric power generation facilities. These facilities use nuclear power to produce electric energy. The electric energy produced in these establishments is provided to electric power transmission systems or to electric power distribution systems.

entries.title: 221114 — Solar Electric Power Generation
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating solar electric power generation facilities. These facilities use energy from the sun to produce electric energy. The electric energy produced in these establishments is provided to electric power transmission systems or to electric power distribution systems.

entries.title: 221115 — Wind Electric Power Generation
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating wind electric power generation facilities. These facilities use wind power to drive a turbine and produce electric energy. The electric energy produced in these establishments is provided to electric power transmission systems or to electric power distribution systems.

entries.title: 221116 — Geothermal Electric Power Generation
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating geothermal electric power generation facilities. These facilities use heat derived from the Earth to produce electric energy. The electric energy produced in these establishments is provided to electric power transmission systems or to electric power distribution systems.

entries.title: 221117 — Biomass Electric Power Generation
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating biomass electric power generation facilities. These facilities use biomass (e.g., wood, waste, alcohol fuels) to produce electric energy. The electric energy produced in these establishments is provided to electric power transmission systems or to electric power distribution systems.

entries.title: 221118 — Other Electric Power Generation
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating electric power generation facilities (except hydroelectric, fossil fuel, nuclear, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). These facilities convert other forms of energy, such as tidal power, into electric energy. The electric energy produced in these establishments is provided to electric power transmission systems or to electric power distribution systems.

entries.title: 22112 — Electric Power Transmission, Control, and Distribution
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating electric power transmission systems, controlling (i.e., regulating voltages) the transmission of electricity, and/or distributing electricity. The transmission system includes lines and transformer stations. These establishments arrange, facilitate, or coordinate the transmission of electricity from the generating source to the distribution centers, other electric utilities, or final consumers. The distribution system …

entries.title: 221121 — Electric Bulk Power Transmission and Control
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating electric power transmission systems and/or controlling (i.e., regulating voltages) the transmission of electricity from the generating source to distribution centers or other electric utilities. The transmission system includes lines and transformer stations.

entries.title: 221122 — Electric Power Distribution
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises electric power establishments primarily engaged in either (1) operating electric power distribution systems (i.e., consisting of lines, poles, meters, and wiring) or (2) operating as electric power brokers or agents that arrange the sale of electricity via power distribution systems operated by others.

entries.title: 2212 — Natural Gas Distribution
entries.excerpt: See industry description for 221210.

entries.title: 22121 — Natural Gas Distribution
entries.excerpt: See industry description for 221210.

entries.title: 221210 — Natural Gas Distribution
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises: (1) establishments primarily engaged in operating gas distribution systems (e.g., mains, meters); (2) establishments known as gas marketers that buy gas from the well and sell it to a distribution system; (3) establishments known as gas brokers or agents that arrange the sale of gas over gas distribution systems operated by others; and (4) establishments primarily engaged in transmitting and distributing gas to final consumers.

entries.title: 2213 — Water, Sewage and Other Systems
entries.excerpt: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in: (1) operating water treatment plants and/or water supply systems; (2) operating sewer systems or sewage treatment facilities; or (3) providing steam, heated air, or cooled air.

entries.title: 22131 — Water Supply and Irrigation Systems
entries.excerpt: See industry description for 221310.

entries.title: 221310 — Water Supply and Irrigation Systems
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in operating water treatment plants and/or operating water supply systems. The water supply system may include pumping stations, aqueducts, and/or distribution mains. The water may be used for drinking, irrigation, or other uses.

entries.title: 22132 — Sewage Treatment Facilities

Waste collection, treatment, and disposal through a sewer system

entries.title: 22133 — Steam and Air-Conditioning Supply

entries.title: 221330 — Steam and Air-Conditioning Supply
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing steam, heated air, or cooled air. The steam distribution may be through mains.

entries.title: 23 — Construction
entries.excerpt: The Construction sector comprises establishments primarily engaged in the construction of buildings or engineering projects (e.g., highways and utility systems). Establishments primarily engaged in the preparation of sites for new construction and establishments primarily engaged in subdividing land for sale as building sites also are included in this sector. Construction work done may include new work, additions, alterations, or maintenance and repairs. Activities of these establishments …

entries.title: 236 — Construction of Buildings
entries.excerpt: The Construction of Buildings subsector comprises establishments primarily responsible for the construction of buildings. The work performed may include new work, additions, alterations, or maintenance and repairs. The on-site assembly of precut, panelized, and prefabricated buildings and construction of temporary buildings are included in this subsector. Part or all of the production work for which the establishments in this subsector have responsibility may be subcontracted to other …

entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily responsible for the construction or remodeling and renovation of single-family and multifamily residential buildings. entries.title: 236117 — New Housing For-Sale Builders
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in building new homes on land that is owned or controlled by the builder rather than the homebuyer or investor. The land is included with the sale of the home. Establishments in this industry build single-family and/or multifamily homes. These establishments are often referred to as merchant builders, but are also known as production or for-sale builders.

entries.title: 48-49 — Transportation and Warehousing
entries.excerpt: The Transportation and Warehousing sector includes industries providing transportation of passengers and cargo, warehousing and storage for goods, scenic and sightseeing transportation, and support activities related to modes of transportation. Establishments in these industries use transportation equipment or transportation-related facilities as a productive asset. The type of equipment depends on the mode of transportation. The modes of transportation are air, rail, water, road, and pipeline. …

entries.title: 481 — Air Transportation
entries.excerpt: Industries in the Air Transportation subsector provide air transportation of passengers and/or cargo using aircraft, such as airplanes, helicopters, and spacecraft. The subsector distinguishes scheduled from nonscheduled air transportation. Scheduled air carriers fly regular routes on regular schedules and operate even if flights are only partially loaded. Nonscheduled carriers often operate during nonpeak time slots at busy airports. These establishments have more flexibility with respect to …

entries.title: 4811 — Scheduled Air Transportation
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing air transportation of passengers and/or cargo over regular routes and on regular schedules. Establishments in this industry operate flights even if partially loaded. Establishments primarily engaged in providing scheduled air transportation of mail on a contract basis are included in this industry.

entries.title: 48111 — Scheduled Air Transportation
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing air transportation of passengers and/or cargo over regular routes and on regular schedules. entries.title: 481111 — Scheduled Passenger Air Transportation
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in providing air transportation of passengers or passengers and freight over regular routes and on regular schedules. Establishments in this industry operate flights even if partially loaded. entries.title: 4812 — Nonscheduled Air Transportation
entries.excerpt: This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in (1) providing air transportation of passengers and/or cargo with no regular routes and regular schedules or (2) providing specialty flying services with no regular routes and regular schedules using general purpose aircraft. These establishments have more flexibility with respect to choice of airports, hours of operation, load factors, and similar operational characteristics.

entries.title: 482 — Rail Transportation
entries.excerpt: Industries in the Rail Transportation subsector provide rail transportation of passengers and/or cargo using railroad rolling stock. The railroads in this subsector primarily either operate on networks, with physical facilities, labor force, and equipment spread over an extensive geographic area, or operate over a short distance on a local rail line. Scenic and sightseeing rail transportation and street railroads, commuter rail, and rapid transit are not included in this subsector but are …

entries.title: 482111 — Line-Haul Railroads
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments known as line-haul railroads primarily engaged in operating railroads for the transport of passengers and/or cargo over a long distance within a rail network. These establishments provide for the intercity movement of trains between the terminals and stations on main and branch lines of a line-haul rail network (except for local switching services).

entries.title: 482112 — Short Line Railroads
entries.excerpt: This U.S. industry comprises establishments known as short-line railroads primarily engaged in operating railroads for the transport of cargo over a short distance on local rail lines not part of a rail network.

entries.title: 483 — Water Transportation
